title: Denmark – Construction work – Slamafvanding ME.04
description: Kalundborg Central Renseanlæg (herefter ”KCR”) skal udvides som en konsekvens af, at industrien i Kalundborg Kommune i de kommende år forøger sin tilledning. Udvidelsen af KCR (herefter ”Projektet”) sker både for at øge den biologiske kapacitet af anlægget, bedre styring af overløb, ny slamafvanding og fjernelse af miljøfremmede stoffer gennem tredje og fjerde renseanlæg. Projektet realiseres gennem en række udbud inden for byggeri- og anlæg, maskin- og el, systemleverandører og SRO. Kalundborg Renseanlæg A/S (”Bygherre”) har indgået en totalrådgiveraftale med Envidan A/S, som forestår teknisk rådgivning og bistand, projektering, byggeledelse og processpecialistrådgivning i forbindelse med Projektets realisering. Dette udbud omfatter en hovedentreprisekontrakt, som i hovedtræk indebærer udførelse af følgende arbejder: • Slamafvanding • Polymeranlæg • Transportøranlæg • Containerløsning for afvandet slam • Slampumper • Slamlagertank • Anlæg for teknisk vand • Trykluftanlæg • Biofilter (luftrensning) • El- og SRO-anlæg for ovenstående Bygningsarbejderne forbundet med at realisere procestrinene udbydes i et særskilt udbud. Tilbudsgiverne skal i tilbudslisten prissætte variable ydelser, herunder reguleringspriser, som kommer til anvendelse, i det omfang, der er behov for. Bygherre har overvejet, om indkøbet kan opdeles yderligere, men vurderer, at en yderligere opdeling vil indebære en række uhensigtsmæssige tekniske og juridiske grænseflader med deraf følgende risiko for forhindringer i udførelsesfasen samt afledte transaktionsomkostninger.

description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Subject to funding, The Cornerstone CIR will solicit prototype fixed-priced proposals for two one Expenditure OTA Agreements with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. The period of performance is estimated to be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. title: USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. description: Section 161 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 laid the groundwork for the development and implementation of remote tower systems (RTSs) to support the modernization of air traffic control services. This initiative aims to explore and deploy RT technology as a cost-effective and efficient alternative to traditional air traffic control towers (ATCTs), particularly in rural and small community airports. The RT program is designed to enhance the FAA's ability to integrate innovative technologies into the National Airspace System (NAS) while maintaining the highest standards of safety and efficiency. RTs provide Visual Flight Rules (VFR) services that extend air traffic control capabilities to underserved areas. The RT program supports the modernization of ATCT infrastructures and promotes cost efficient tower solutions at VFR airports within the (NAS). The program facilitates the evaluation and deployment of RTs, ensuring that they seamlessly transition into real-world operational environments. This initiative supports the FAA's mission to modernize air traffic management and maintain safety and efficiency across the NAS. Under FAA direction and safety oversight, selected airports will integrate and operationalize RT technology, leveraging the insights gained from the System Design Approval (SDA) at the Tech Center. Additional research goals and objectives for government-funded activities may be outlined for sites in specific tasks under the IDIQ. This will help the government evaluate and improve RT technologies in its efforts to continually improve the safety and efficiency of the NAS. This will support the collection and analysis of data essential for: 1. Optimizing RT operations within a multi-runway operational environment. 2. Evaluating the performance and reliability of remote sensing and communication technologies under varied operational conditions. 3. Assessing the infrastructure requirements and scalability of RTS in broader deployment and diverse airport settings. 4. Collecting operational data to inform future policy, safety approvals and implementation decisions. Justification for a Direct Award is summarized as follows: Frequentis (FRQ) is an established global provider of air traffic management and RT solutions. FRQ has deployed digital tower systems internationally and specializes in mission-critical communication and control systems for aviation environments. FRQ has worked in coordination with the FAA and the William J. Hughes Technical Center to develop, and configure, a RTS aligned with FAA safety, human factors, and operational requirements. The FRQ RTS is the only solution that has progressed through the FAA�s SDA process to date. While other vendors offer RT technologies globally, no other system has achieved comparable advancement within the FAA�s design approval and integration framework. Selecting an alternative vendor at this stage would require duplicative design approval activities, additional technical evaluation, and extended safety validation, resulting in significant schedule delays and increased program costs. The program�s reason to establish the RT Program is to comply with Section 621 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, which mandates the development and deployment of RT technologies. This initiative aims to enhance air traffic management capabilities at rural and small community airports by integrating advanced RTSs into the NAS. The program is also supporting FAA strategic objectives to modernize the NAS through implementation of innovative, scalable, and cost-effective technologies. RTSs provide a viable alternative to traditional air traffic control infrastructure, enabling expanded service capabilities while optimizing resource utilization across a diverse range of airport environments. Currently, FRQ is the only vendor with a technically acceptable system to comply with the Reauthorization Act of 2024. To meet the requirements, the FAA must leverage the only system that has achieved the necessary level of technical maturity and alignment with FAA standards. While the FAA is actively conducting outreach to additional vendors to participate in the SDA process, onboarding and evaluating alternative systems will require additional time for design approval, testing and validation, and will not support immediate program timelines.

description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit white paper proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. DFARS clause 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. Contractors may obtain Cornerstone registration information located at https://cornerstone.army.mil or by inquiring at: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil. Interested parties should stay alert for any changes that may be published to this sam.gov posting. description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. description: The primary objective of this work under Solicitation Number N3943026R5001 is to establish a scientifically sound methodology to quantify and evaluate per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) distributions in precipitation, ambient fog water, and ambient soils at multiple active U.S. Navy installations. title: Belgium – Church construction work – Restauration de la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre
description: Les présents travaux portent sur la restauration de l’enveloppe extérieure ainsi que sur l’intérieur de la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre. L’objectif de cette restauration est d’assurer la pérennité de l’édifice tout en conservant ses caractéristiques actuelles et ses différentes strates archéologiques. Les travaux comprennent également la rationalisation et la mise aux normes des installations techniques afin que la Basilique puisse continuer à être utilisée comme lieu de culte. Le marché est divisé en deux lots : > Lot 1 - Restauration de l'enveloppe extérieure et intérieure : Ce lot comprend l'installation de chantier générale, les toitures, façades, menuiseries extérieures et les travaux intérieurs > Lot 2 - Restauration des vitraux : Ce lot comprend toutes les interventions propres aux vitraux La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre est classée comme Monument suivant l'arrêté royal du 08/03/1938. Philosophie d’intervention : La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre telle que nous l’observons aujourd’hui est le résultat de modifications et d’agrandissements s’étalant sur huit siècles consécutifs avec une dernière transformation majeure au 18ème siècle réalisée vraisemblablement par l’architecte de la cour Guillaume De Bruyne. Cette dernière transformation a changé irrévocablement la morphologie de l’édifice de telle sorte qu’il n’est plus possible de revenir à une situation antérieure. Les travaux exécutés au 18ème siècle ont été marqués par une volonté d’uniformisation de l’église avec le souhait d’une plus grande harmonie dans la lecture de l’édifice de manière à le voir comme un ensemble et non plus comme l’adjonction d’éléments de différentes époques (construction du collatéral sud sur base du collatéral nord, façade ouest travaillée symétriquement, etc.). L’édifice conserve toutefois dans ses maçonneries, les traces subtiles de son évolution au cours des siècles comme autant de strates successives. Chaque rénovation/transformation a ajouté une nouvelle couche avec les moyens et le style de son époque. Notre philosophie d’intervention s’inscrit dans une volonté de préserver ces différentes strates successives comme témoignage à la fois historique et archéologique de l’évolution du bâti. Nous opterons pour une restauration respectueuse des matériaux et de la morphologie actuelle de l’édifice avec ses irrégularités et ses variations. Une attention spécifique sera portée aux ouvrages anciens, à leur typologie, à leurs caractéristiques, à leur identité afin de proposer des interventions les valorisant pour les générations futures. Plus précisément, quatre critères cadrent notre philosophie de restauration et de rénovation pour la Basilique. Ces critères servent de fils conducteur pour déterminer les options d’intervention sur les divers ouvrages. Pour chaque nouvelle option à prendre, nous vérifierons qu’elle se situe dans la continuité de cette philosophie de manière à atteindre une unité dans les interventions à prévoir. Les quatre critères pour la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre sont les suivants :  La préservation/sauvegarde de l’édifice dans son état actuel (pas de retour vers un état antérieur, pas de démolitions), préservation des matériaux et du mode constructif, sauvegarde des différentes strates/couches archéologiques ;  La pérennité/stabilité des interventions proposées par une remise en état des ouvrages selon la situation actuelle et si nécessaire, la mise en œuvre de protections ou d’améliorations contemporaines spécifiques en vue de créer les conditions optimales de préservation et de durabilité et ce, dans le respect des valeurs patrimoniales des éléments constitutifs ;  L’optimisation des coûts en intervenant sur les questions prioritaires pouvant avoir un impact sur la pérennité/conservation des ouvrages mais sans reconstituer les éléments disparus ou n’ayant qu’un intérêt purement esthétique ;  La garantie de pouvoir utiliser le bâtiment selon son usage actuel et de façon optimale. La proposition s’oriente donc vers une « Restauration-conservatoire » dans le sens où nous cherchons à restaurer les propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles (d’un ouvrage, des matériaux) nécessaires à la conservation durable/pérenne du bâtiment. La restauration des propriétés structurelles et fonctionnelles d’un ouvrage ou des matériaux se fait soit par remplacement/réparation/consolidation, soit par la mise en place d’une protection.

title: Belgium – Church construction work – Restauration de la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre
description: Les présents travaux portent sur la restauration de l’enveloppe extérieure ainsi que sur l’intérieur de la Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre. L’objectif de cette restauration est d’assurer la pérennité de l’édifice tout en conservant ses caractéristiques actuelles et ses différentes strates archéologiques. Les travaux comprennent également la rationalisation et la mise aux normes des installations techniques afin que la Basilique puisse continuer à être utilisée comme lieu de culte. Le marché est divisé en deux lots : > Lot 1 - Restauration de l'enveloppe extérieure et intérieure : Ce lot comprend l'installation de chantier générale, les toitures, façades, menuiseries extérieures et les travaux intérieurs > Lot 2 - Restauration des vitraux : Ce lot comprend toutes les interventions propres aux vitraux La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre est classée comme Monument suivant l'arrêté royal du 08/03/1938. Philosophie d’intervention : La Basilique Notre-Dame de Basse-Wavre telle que nous l’observons aujourd’hui est le résultat de modifications et d’agrandissements s’étalant sur huit siècles consécutifs avec une dernière transformation majeure au 18ème siècle réalisée vraisemblablement par l’architecte de la cour Guillaume De Bruyne. Cette dernière transformation a changé irrévocablement la morphologie de l’édifice de telle sorte qu’il n’est plus possible de revenir à une situation antérieure. Les travaux exécutés au 18ème siècle ont été marqués par une volonté d’uniformisation de l’église avec le souhait d’une plus grande harmonie dans la lecture de l’édifice de manière à le voir comme un ensemble et non plus comme l’adjonction d’éléments de différentes époques (construction du collatéral sud sur base du collatéral nord, façade ouest travaillée symétriquement, etc.). L’édifice conserve toutefois dans ses maçonneries, les traces subtiles de son évolution au cours des siècles comme autant de strates successives. Chaque rénovation/transformation a ajouté une nouvelle couche avec les moyens et le style de son époque. Notre philosophie d’intervention s’inscrit dans une volonté de préserver ces différentes strates successives comme témoignage à la fois historique et archéologique de l’évolution du bâti. Nous opterons pour une restauration respectueuse des matériaux et de la morphologie actuelle de l’édifice avec ses irrégularités et ses variations. Une attention spécifique sera portée aux ouvrages anciens, à leur typologie, à leurs caractéristiques, à leur identité afin de proposer des interventions les valorisant pour les générations futures. Plus précisément, quatre critères cadrent notre philosophie de restauration et de rénovation pour la Basilique. Ces critères servent de fils conducteur pour déterminer les options d’intervention sur les divers ouvrages. Pour chaque nouvelle option à prendre, nous vérifierons qu’elle se situe dans la continuité de cette philosophie de manière à atteindre une unité dans les interventions à prévoir.
